Subject: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & SDK next steps for ACME

Hi Sanjay  thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: integrate Redwood inference into ACME's internal app for document search and reranking, with embeddings stored in a private posture.
- Networking constraints: ACME prefers private connectivity (no public egress for inference calls), static IPs for allowlist, and mTLS between services where possible.
- Auth & SDK: you prefer short-lived tokens for app calls; you also asked about client certificate support.

Open items / asks
1) Network topology: can you share a simple diagram showing whether you want AWS PrivateLink, VPC peering, or a shared NAT egress? We attached a proposed topology PNG.
2) IP allowlist: we can provide static egress IP ranges for Dedicated/Private setups; need confirmation on whether ACME needs single static IP or a CIDR block.
3) mTLS: clarify if you want mutual TLS to terminate at a private endpoint inside your VPC or if you prefer us to terminate and present a client cert.
4) Embeddings: confirm whether embeddings should be stored on Redwood-managed storage (encrypted at rest) or kept inside your VPC (Private deployment).

Next steps (proposed)
- Marissa: can you follow up with a short tech note including sample SDK config, auth options (token vs mutual cert), and the IP/FQDN info we can provide?
- Sanjay: if you can share the network diagram and any existing firewall/NAT requirements by EOD Monday, well prepare a technical deep dive.
- Schedule: propose Thu 6/24 for a technical deep dive (3045m) with ACME infra + Redwood SEs.

Attachments: acme-proposed-topology.png (attached), sample SDK snippet coming from Marissa.

Thanks  Jonas

--

Thanks, Jonas  helpful recap. A few clarifying Qs from my side before the deep dive:

1) Which Redwood deployment modes support keeping embeddings inside our VPC? We want vector storage to never leave our network.
2) For the hosted API option, can you confirm whether mutual TLS is available for inbound calls from our NAT (we would prefer cert-based auth rather than IP-only).
3) Static IPs: we need a single static egress IP for outbound calls so our firewall team can set rules. Is that possible for a hosted plan or only for Dedicated/Private?
4) Data residency: do logs or traces ever flow to external regions for observability? We need US-only for this workload.

I'll circulate a network sketch but we are leaning toward Private deployment if embedding storage can be locked in our VPC.

Hi Sanjay  thanks for the clear questions. Outline below addresses each ask; Ive attached our VPC setup guide and a sample SDK config script.

1) Embeddings persistence– Private deployment options: we support embedding storage entirely inside the customer's VPC when you choose Redwood Private (VPC-hosted control plane or on-prem packaging). This keeps vectors on your subnets and behind your KMS if desired.
- Hosted API: embeddings are stored in Redwood-managed encrypted storage (AES-256), and we can offer contractual controls and region restrictions but the data is outside your VPC.

2) mTLS and certificate options– Private deployment: mutual TLS is supported end-to-end. You can present client certs to our private endpoint inside your network or we can exchange certs across a peered endpoint.
- Hosted with PrivateLink: we can front a PrivateLink endpoint that accepts client certificate authentication; however, for fully managed hosted tiers default is token-based. If you need cert-based auth + IP allowlist, we recommend Dedicated with PrivateLink.

3) Static IP / egress– Single static IP is not available for the public hosted tier. For deterministic static egress we offer: Dedicated (reserved capacity) with a small NAT pool you control, or Private deployment where your NAT/egress addresses are customer-managed. We can also support a small set of static egress IPs for marketplace/Dedicated customers  Ill include ranges in the attached doc.

4) Data residency and observability– We support region restrictions on logs and traces for Dedicated/Private customers. For Hosted, traces are kept in the US by default for US deployments; if you need contractual assurances and audit controls we recommend Dedicated/Private.

5) SDK & auth patterns– Hosted: short-lived bearer tokens (recommended for web/mobile flows). SDKs support automatic refresh and built-in retries.
- Private: you can use mutual TLS or token auth combined with private routing. I attached sample-sdk-config.sh with example token + mTLS settings and sample HTTP routing for model fallbacks.

6) Routing, structured output, and tool-calling– Routing: we support region-based routing and policy-based fallbacks (e.g., if primary model is overloaded, route to a quantized variant).
- Structured Output & tool calling: supported in both Hosted and Dedicated. For Private we can set up internal tool runners inside your VPC for zero egress.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-setup-guide.pdf (contains PrivateLink, peering, IP ranges); sample-sdk-config.sh (example token & cert configs).

Suggested next step
- Technical deep dive: Thu 6/24 10:0010:45 PT. Ill bring the network checklist and a short runbook for embedding storage options.

If you want earlier answers to firewall rules or a specific CIDR for allowlisting, tell me your preference for PrivateLink vs peering and Ill send the exact values.

Best,
Marissa
